title: Ab urbe condita
author: Livy

passages.original: ludi quam amplissimi ut fierent senatus decrevit. ad eos ludos auctore Attio Tullio vis magna Volscorum venit.
passages.english: The senate decreed that the games should be held on the most lavish scale possible. To these games, at the instigation of Attius Tullius, a great number of Volscians came.

passages.original: secundum Hieronymi caedem primo tumultuatum in Leontinis apud milites fuerat vociferatumque ferociter parentandum regi sanguine coniuratorum esse.
passages.english: After the murder of Hieronymus there had at first been an uproar among the soldiers at Leontini, and they had shouted fiercely that the king's shade must be appeased with the blood of the conspirators.
passages.notes: 'parentandum regi sanguine' literally 'offerings must be made to the [dead] king with blood', the language of funeral offerings to the dead.

passages.original: prima forte signa sescentorum Cretensium erant, qui apud Hieronymum meruerant sub eis et Hannibalis beneficium habebant, capti ad Trasumennum inter Romanorum auxilia dimissique.
passages.english: By chance the leading standards were those of six hundred Cretans, who had served under Hieronymus among them and were under obligation for a kindness from Hannibal, having been captured at Trasimene among the auxiliaries of the Romans and released.
passages.notes: 'apud Hieronymum meruerant sub eis' is awkward; 'sub eis' ('under them') may be corrupt. The sense may be that they had served with Hieronymus among the troops in question.
